question: How are NYC crashes distributed across the days of the week, 2013 to 2025?

initial_plan.can_answer: yes, the file has one record per police-reported crash and a crash date from which weekday can be derived
initial_plan.population: one record per police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash with a nonmissing crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive
initial_plan.grouping: day of week derived from crash_date, Monday through Sunday

data_check.findings: The selected population has 2,132,218 dated crash records. There are 0 missing or impossible crash_date values among included rows; crash_date is a DATE, so empty strings and text unknown codes are not representable. All years 2013-2025 run from January 1 through December 31 in the file.
data_check.decision: Keep all in-range dated records. Records with no usable date or dates outside 2013-2025 cannot be assigned to the requested period and are not counted; missing-date rows cannot be assigned to a year.

final_plan.can_answer: yes, for police-reported crash records with a usable crash_date in the requested period
final_plan.population: one record per police-reported NYC motor vehicle crash with a nonmissing crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive
final_plan.years: 2013-2025 inclusive; each calendar year is present from January 1 through December 31
final_plan.grouping: day of week derived from crash_date, Monday through Sunday
final_plan.limitations: Counts describe police-reported crash records, not crash risk per day or exposure-adjusted rates; crashes with no usable date cannot be assigned to this period, and no date-missing rows occur in the included population.
